items.rootCause: Server side (apps/server/src/rooms/GameRoom.ts). The client gets the others' avatars and flags from only two places. In a friends room they come from the `lobby` message, whose seats carry avatarId and country (OnlineSession.profiles -> profilesOfLobby). In ranked they come from 'found', or from the record ranked resume keeps on the phone. When an app comes back into a running game on a NEW connection (the loop-8 takeover of a held seat after a process kill, or the loop-9 cold-start resume), GameRoom.onJoin -> welcomeBack sent only the snapshot (and the solution after the end), never the lobby. The new process had kept nothing of the lobby it saw before, so session.profiles was null. GameScreen, the lock avatars, OpponentLeft and the results' 'יריב' card then drew the grey NO_AVATAR silhouette with no flag until the end. Ranked has the same gap wherever no profiles are passed in. One example is match/index 'back to the game' (rejoinRankedGame without profiles): a match room's lobby carried only id and name.
items.fix: GameRoom.welcomeBack now sends the room's `lobby` to the returning connection. It goes after the snapshot, or after the `countdown` when there is no game yet, and never before it: a lobby with no game and no count is what the app shows as the waiting room. sendLobby is split into sendLobbyTo(client, seat, content). A friends room's lobby already carries each seat's avatarId and country (FriendsLobby.view(), which after the start holds the game's seats). A match room's lobby now carries them too: RankedMatchPlayer has optional avatarId and country, which matchmaking's claim() fills from the same stored player that 'found' used (persona included), and GameRoom.lobbyContent adds them. No change to the protocol types (LobbyPlayer already had the optional fields), and no client code change. RemoteGameHost already stores a lobby that comes while a game is running and notifies online. GameScreen subscribes to online info and reads session.profiles on each render, so the card updates even when the lobby arrives after the board is up. Older apps handle the extra message the same way. The ranked cold-start resume path (its stored profiles take precedence) is unchanged.
items.test: Server: apps/server/test/friendsRoom.test.ts 'mid-game, the app killed and opened again…' now also expects a `lobby` after the snapshot on the new connection, with Cy's card {avatarId 'noam', country 'IL'}. apps/server/test/matchmaking.test.ts 'the app killed mid-game and opened again…' expects the same for ranked: Kai's {avatarId 'lava-lamp', country 'IL'} after the snapshot. Both fail on the old code: I disabled the line and got 'no lobby within 4000 ms; got snapshot, events', then restored it. stealth/matchmaking.test.ts was updated: the match setup's players now carry the card. Client: the fake friends server (net/testing/fakeFriends.ts) now mirrors welcomeBack, sending the snapshot and then the lobby. The new apps/mobile/src/screens/game/__tests__/rejoinCards.test.tsx has two cases, both through OnlineGame/GameScreen with a FakeFriendsTable whose game is already running. (a) The cold return: session.profiles has NinaVolt {pirate, DE}, and card-opponent shows avatar 'pirate' and flag-DE. (b) The lobby held back until the game screen is up: grey with no flag first, then avatar and flag once the lobby lands. Both fail with the old fake behaviour (verified). All server room, matchmaking and stealth suites pass (39 suites). So do the mobile net, friends, roomLinks, GameScreenOnline and rankedResume suites. tsc (mobile and server) and eslint are clean.

Friends: Phone 1 creates a friends room (מהיר); Phone 3 joins with the code; Phone 1 presses 'התחל משחק · 2 שחקנים'. items.rootCause: The friends joiner, right after a cold start, came in by a code or link straight into the room's lobby. It never passed the game type screen or a ranked search. Those two are where the first game of a run is made ready (screens/match/warmGame.ts, QA K2). So its first game paid, under GO!, for building the game screen's ~13 sound players (expo-audio builds each on the UI thread while the JS thread blocks: no frame and no JS meanwhile, docs/PERF.md T3-FIRST-PLAY-SLOW) and for loading the game screen's code. It also built the 'countdownBeat' and 'go' players on their first play. app/friends/room.tsx only opens /game after GO! has held friendsGoHoldMs (250 ms on Android), so all of that work stretched GO! to ~2.1 s. Ranked had exactly the same pattern before K2: 1.75 s on the first game, 1.0–1.1 s later. The ~0.9–1.0 s seen in later games and on the host is the game screen's own mount and first draw on the A16 plus the stack fade. motion.md accepts that for ranked ('a phone slower to draw the game keeps GO! on screen meanwhile'). It is not addressed here.
items.fix: warmGame.ts: new FRIENDS_COUNT_CUES (countdownBeat, go) and warmFriendsGameSteps(). The steps are the game screen's sounds, then its code (loadGameCode), then the count's two players. app/friends/room.tsx: while the room's phase is 'lobby', it runs warmGameLater(warmFriendsGameSteps): 400 ms after entering, one step per idle moment. It stops as soon as the phase leaves the lobby (count started, game, closed), so nothing is built under 3-2-1 or GO!. The GO hold, the GO! frame before the board (loop 8) and the Back gate are unchanged, so the empty frame and the faded '1' do not come back. With sound off, no players are made (only the code is loaded). No strings changed; no animation added (Reduced Motion is unaffected).

(1) In the lobby (Dana in, waiting for 'התחל'), every player of GAME_CUES and the count's two is made and the game screen's code is required once. Then 3-2-1, GO! and the move to /game make no new player. This fails with the warm-up disabled in the route (verified, then restored). (2) The step order: sounds, code, the count's two. warmGame.test, friendsRoutes, roomPhase, FriendsRoomScreen, startupGraph and reducedMotion pass; tsc and eslint are clean.

rep.notes: Item 1 is a server-only fix: it needs a staging deploy, but no APK. The returning connection now gets `lobby` right after `snapshot` (or after `countdown`), never before it. Before it would briefly show the friends waiting room on a cold resume, because friends.ts phaseOf gives 'lobby' for status lobby + lobby + playerId. Match rooms' lobby now carries avatarId and country from the matchmaking store (also for a stealth persona: the same card 'found' showed), so ranked 'back to the game' (match/index rejoinRankedGame with no profiles) gets the cards too. No protocol type changed. Item 2 is marked partial on purpose. The cold-start extra (sound players and game code built under GO!) is removed, the same cure as ranked K2. The remaining ~0.9–1.0 s in steady state is the game screen's own mount and first draw plus the stack fade. Cutting that to 0.25–0.5 s would need the ranked GoCover handoff (push /game over the room screen and keep GO! drawn over the mounting game). That is a larger change, across app/game.tsx, goHandoff and the room route, that other agents' files touch. If the host presses start within ~1 s of the joiner entering, the warm-up may not finish, and whatever is left is built as before. Tests run: 39 server suites (rooms, matchmaking, stealth, e2e contracts) plus the mobile net, friends, GameScreenOnline, rankedResume, warmGame, startupGraph and reducedMotion suites, all green. tsc for mobile and server and eslint on the changed files are clean. Prettier was run on the changed files only. No strings were added, so no i18n check was needed. No adb, build, deploy, git or npm install.

issues.problem: Side effect of item 1 in the countdown branch: a returning connection now gets `lobby` while state is still null. RemoteGameHost's lobby handler takes the 'Back in a lobby after a drop' branch: it sets lost=null and comingBack=null and moves status to 'lobby'. For a token reconnect during a ranked or friends 3-2-1, the 'resyncing' state ends early. When the snapshot comes at GO there is no `lost`, so there is no hard/soft decision, no resyncedAt banner, and the reconnect telemetry (trackSafely 'reconnect', metrics.cameBack) is never sent for that return. The UI is the same as a normal countdown: status 'lobby' plus startsAt. friends phaseOf gives 'countdown' first, and inFriendsLobby() is false because startsAt is set. So nothing breaks for the user.
issues.evidence: apps/server/src/rooms/GameRoom.ts welcomeBack: `if (this.phase === 'countdown') { this.sendCountdown(client); this.sendLobbyTo(client, seat); }`. In apps/mobile/src/net/remoteGameHost.ts:812-818, `if (this.state) this.notifyOnline(); else { this.lost = null; this.comingBack = null; this.setStatus('lobby'); }`. In onSnapshot (911-929), the banner and the comingBack metrics depend on `this.lost` and `this.comingBack`.
issues.suggestion: Not blocking. Accept it, or send the countdown-phase lobby only on a new connection (onJoin takeover), not from onReconnect. The token path keeps the session's lobby in memory, so it already has the cards.

issues.problem: Item 2 is honestly marked partial, and the cause is not yet shown on a device. The warm-up builds only the sound players and the game code. A cold process on the A16 may also pay for other first-time work under GO!: the first draw of the avatar art and SVGs, font and asset loading, Reanimated worklet init, and the hit cues. If that is the bulk of the extra ~1.1 s, GO! will still be long. The warm-up also needs ~16 idle steps after a 400 ms delay. If the host presses start within ~1–2 s of the joiner entering, part of the work still lands under 3-2-1/GO. Each expo-audio player blocks the UI thread, so the lobby (on both phones, since the host warms too) gets up to ~15 short stalls. The ranked search already accepts the same stalls.
issues.evidence: apps/mobile/app/friends/room.tsx:88-89 `useEffect(() => (inLobby ? warmGameLater(warmFriendsGameSteps) : undefined), [inLobby])`. warmGame.ts warmFriendsGameSteps = GAME_CUES players + loadGameCode + countdownBeat/go. The QA item (docs/handoff/2026-11-03/data/fixcheck-apk14.json) gives only the timings (2.1 s cold joiner, 1.0 s later, 0.9 s host), with no profile. The host also reaches the room without the game type screen (ModesScreen -> /friends/room?create=1), so the 0.9 s host figure most likely comes from a phone that was already warm.
issues.suggestion: Keep it, and let the device check (new APK, joiner waits at least 3 s in the lobby) decide. If GO! is still well over ~1.0 s on a cold joiner, profile the first /game mount (systrace or Hermes profiler) before adding more to the warm-up. The real fix to 0.25–0.5 s is still the GoCover handoff for friends.

items.rootCause: I couldn't reproduce this off the device. These are the two causes I found in the code, and they match the frames. (1) Each layer of a hit ran its own clock. BoardHitLayer (the dim), HitLayer (the overlay and banner) and the two WarpFrames (the tilt) each called useHitClock, so there were 4 frame callbacks, each started and anchored on its own. Nothing tied them to one frame, which explains why the order changed between runs: dim first with sound on, overlay first with sound off. (2) The start cue played inside the commit's effects (useHitFeedback onStart). On Android, expo-audio runs `play` as runBlocking on the main queue (AudioModule.kt runOnMain), so the JS thread waits for the UI thread. That wait came before react-native-worklets' microtask handed the hit's start to the UI thread (the clock start, setActive, the layers' styles). So with sound on, the start of the visuals waited behind the sound. The players themselves are already preloaded since loop 8 (useWarmHitCues), and this phone uses mixWithOthers, so there is no audio-focus request.
items.fix: (1) One clock per hit. GameScreen now makes a single `hitElapsed = useHitClock(isHitOn(hit, now) ? hit : null, session.clock)` and passes it as a new optional `elapsed` prop to both WarpFrames, BoardHitLayer and HitLayer. A new useLayerHitClock(hit, clock, shared) in components/interference/hitClock.ts returns the shared clock when one is given, and the layer's own clock otherwise (used when a layer runs alone, in tests or the gallery). The dim, the overlay, the banner's ring and fade-out, and the tilt now read the same value in the same UI frame. WarpFrame still tilts only for an active warp in its region. (2) The cue plays after the visuals' start. In useHitFeedback, the start cue goes through a new afterUiStart(): two promise microtasks, so it runs after the worklets flush, still within the same JS turn, with no timer. The rumble and the announcement are unchanged. A hit that ends before its cue plays gets no cue, which also stops a double cue under StrictMode. Reduced Motion is unchanged: the same static cover, the same fades and the start Warning, all from the same single clock.
items.test: New file apps/mobile/src/screens/game/hit/__tests__/hitStartTogether.test.tsx. (a) WarpFrame, BoardHitLayer and HitLayer get a shared clock at 120 ms while the game clock is 2 s into the hit. The dim's opacity is 0.3 (half of its fade-in) and there is no tilt. When the shared clock moves to 3.5 s, the dim is at full 0.6, the ring shows '2' (its own clock would say '3'), and the tilt has started. On the old code the prop is ignored and each layer follows its own clock, so this fails. (b) The hit is committed inside a synchronous React act, which runs the effects but no microtasks. No cue has played yet; after the microtasks, exactly ['hitWarp'] has played. On the old code the cue plays inside the commit, so this fails. (c) A hit removed before its cue played gives no cue. All of these pass: HitLayer, BoardHitLayer, HitBanner, warmHitCues, useKeypadShuffle, GameScreenDuel, interferenceKinds, components/interference and workletClosures (122 + suites). tsc and eslint are clean.
items.deviceCheck: Receiver phone with sound ON and Reduce Motion off. Start a new 2-player friends or ranked game (fresh app start is best). Wait at least 3 s after the board appears. Then the sender sends 'עיוות' as the first hit of the game. Record the receiver with screenrecord and step through at 10–20 ms. You should see that the board dim, the brown overlay with its waves and the banner drop all start within the same frame or the next one. There must be no stretch of dim alone and no stretch of overlay alone. The tilt starts only after the fade-in, about 0.24 s later. The sound arrives with the visuals, at most one or two frames after them. Repeat with sound OFF: same picture, everything starts together. Repeat with 'דיו' and 'זיקוקים' as the first hit. Send a second hit in the same game: it fades in from the start with no pop. Then turn Reduce Motion ON in the app and send 'עיוות': the static cover, the dim and the banner fade in together, with no wave movement. If a gap still shows, take a logcat around the hit (look for Choreographer 'Skipped N frames') and record which layer came first.

items.id: misc#1 results rating card visible / count
items.rootCause: On a 1080x2340 phone with 3-button navigation (about 411x891 dp), after an abandon win the hero has two tags, 'מקום 1 מתוך 2' and 'ניצחת בנטישה', plus the long end line 'היריב איבד חיבור ולא חזר בזמן'. Below them come the final score and the opponent card. Together these push the rating card's number row about 55 dp below the ScrollView's bottom edge, where the action bar is a flex sibling. Loop 8's gate (useScrolledIntoView) does hold the count until the number is in view: the geometry is right for this layout too (the block is a direct child of the content, and the row is a direct child of the card). But nothing brought the number into view, so the user had to scroll. During a slow scroll the count starts as soon as the row's bottom crosses the edge and finishes in 0.65 s, which is why QA saw it already at 1286. Shrinking the layout without going under the design sizes would not save 55 dp: the content gaps of 24 dp are the design's, and the avatar must stay at profile size per spec §12.
items.fix: useScrolledIntoView now also gives the ScrollView a ref, watches onScrollBeginDrag, and returns reveal(margin, animated). A new pure helper, revealOffset(), computes how far to scroll so the row's bottom ends `margin` above the edge. It returns null when no scroll is needed, or when the scroll would be more than REVEAL_MAX_SHARE (40%) of the view's height. ResultsBody calls reveal(space[8], true) at victory.ratingCountAt (+1200 ms, after the hero and crown have landed), only in a rated game and not under Reduced Motion. It does nothing once the number has been seen or once the user has dragged. So on this phone the view glides up about 70 dp, the onScroll events mark the number as seen, and it then counts from the old rating to the new one in view. This works for every ending: abandon, surrender, full board, 2P. A 4P ranking that is too long is left to the user's scroll, and the gate still holds the count until the number is seen. No text sizes or design spacing changed, and no strings were added. I updated the motion.md rating.count row.
items.test: apps/mobile/src/screens/results/__tests__/resultsRanked.test.tsx has a new describe block with 3 tests. (a) Scroll view 700 high, card at 650, number ending at 730. At 1199 ms there is no scrollTo. At 1200 ms there is exactly one scrollTo({ y: 30 + space[8], animated: true }), and the value still shows the old rating. After that scroll offset arrives, the count reaches the new rating. On the old code there is no scrollTo, so this fails. (b) After onScrollBeginDrag there is no auto-scroll. revealOffset returns null when the number is too far, already in view, or not measured, and returns 76 for a 20 / 700 / 760 / 16 case. (c) Under Reduced Motion there is no scroll and the new rating shows at once. The existing loop-8 tests still pass: count waits below the fold, and in view the count runs at 1200. All results suites pass (21/21 in resultsRanked, plus resultsFit, ResultsDuel, resultsOnline and the others).
items.deviceCheck: Use the A16 (1080x2340, 3-button nav), in Hebrew, with Reduce Motion off. Play a ranked 'מהיר' 2-player game and win by abandon (the opponent's phone goes to airplane mode until 'ניצחת בנטישה'). On the results screen, don't touch anything. At about 1.2 s the screen should glide up a little, about 70 dp: the avatar slides partly under the status bar, and the title and tags stay visible. Warp: I couldn't reproduce the timing off the device. issues.problem: Item 1 (warp, sound on, dim before overlay): the fix probably does not change what the phone shows. Neither cause the fixer names can make the dim start before the overlay and banner.
issues.evidence: (a) On the old code, each layer's useHitClock effect ran in the same passive-effects flush. Every shared-value `.set` and `frame.setActive` goes through `scheduleOnUI` → `enqueueUI`, which pushes into one queue that a single `queueMicrotask` flushes (react-native-worklets 0.10.1, threads.native.ts:340-360; reanimated 4.5.1, mutables.ts:216-224 and FrameCallbackRegistryJS.ts:35-38). So all four clocks reached the UI thread in one batch. Each one anchors on its first `info.timestamp`, which is the same frame for all of them, and its `base` comes from clock.now() taken microseconds apart. Four clocks could not drift 170 ms apart. (b) The banner's visibility does not follow the hit clock at all. In HitBanner.tsx:96-102, opacity = min(1, enter) × fade-out, and `enter` is its own withSpring started in its own effect. A shared clock cannot move the banner relative to the dim, and the fixer's own notes admit this. (c) Moving `play` after the flush only changes when the clock start is posted relative to the runBlocking `play` on the main looper (AudioModule.kt:467-480, runOnMain = runBlocking(mainQueue)). The next vsync waits for `play` in both orders, so every layer is delayed by the same amount and the gap between them stays. (d) The symptom shows only on the first hit of a game, and the dim (one plain Animated.View) shows first. That points to the cost of mounting HitLayer's new subtree on the first hit: a Skia Canvas (WarpOverlay, whose TextureView surface arrives a frame or more later), react-native-svg in the CountdownRing, an AnimatedTextInput, and AvatarArt, which sets state from timers (Jest shows act() warnings from AvatarArt.tsx:389). Nothing in the change addresses this. The new test hitStartTogether.test.tsx only proves that the `elapsed` prop reaches the layers and that the cue moved to a microtask. It cannot show the order of frames on the phone. Tests, tsc and eslint all pass.
issues.suggestion: Don't mark this as fixed until a screenrecord on the phone confirms it. Fix the likely cause instead: keep HitLayer's effect canvas and banner mounted but invisible (opacity 0, no hit) from the time the game screen mounts, so the first hit mounts no views and the Skia surface already exists. Do this as a warm-up, like useWarmHitCues. If that is not enough, also hold the shared clock (and with it the dim) until HitLayer reports it is ready, for example from the onLayout of its region view or of the Canvas. Drive the banner's entry from the shared clock (for example a worklet curve over HIT_FADE_IN_MS) instead of its own spring, so all three really do read one clock in the same frame. Keep the Reduced Motion path: a static cover with the same fade.

issues.problem: Performance regression: during every hit kind (fireworks, cats, ink, scramble, keypad), both WarpFrames now push a transform to the native views on every frame for the full 5 s. Before the change this happened only during a warp, and only for the active region.
issues.evidence: WarpFrame now reads the shared `hitElapsed`, which runs for any hit (GameScreen.tsx:1139; Warp.tsx:86, which notes 'The shared clock runs for any hit'). useAnimatedStyle takes its inputs from the worklet's closure, so the mapper runs on every frame that `elapsed` changes, even though the worklet returns early when `!active`. That early return gives `{ transform: warpTransform(NO_WARP) }`, and warpTransform allocates a new array on each call (warpModel.ts:98-107). Reanimated compares the new style with shallowEqual (useAnimatedStyle.ts:304; utils.ts:20-35), so the new array never matches and updateProps runs every frame on the screen-root content view and on the board. Before the change, the inactive WarpFrame's own clock was idle (hit = null).
issues.suggestion: In WarpFrame, use the shared clock only while that frame is active: `useLayerHitClock(active ? hit : null, clock, active ? shared : undefined)`, so an inactive frame keeps an idle clock of its own. Also return a cached identity transform, so a style that has not changed is not sent again.

issues.problem: Item 2 (rating card): the results screen scrolls by itself 1.2 s after it opens, even when TalkBack is on. The count's visual is irrelevant to a TalkBack user, and the jump can move content under the accessibility focus.
issues.evidence: ResultsScreen.tsx:277-282 checks only `rated` and `reduce` before calling reveal(space[8], true). Otherwise the item looks right. I checked the gate: the rating block is a direct child of the content and the row is a direct child of the card, so the measured bottom is correct. No text sizes changed. resultsRanked passes 21/21, and all 28 related suites pass (418 tests).
issues.suggestion: Skip the reveal while a screen reader is on: check AccessibilityInfo.isScreenReaderEnabled, or reuse a hook the app already has. Keep the existing gate, which holds the count until the number is seen.

They could not drift 170 ms apart, so they were not the cause. The single shared clock stays in, but it is clean-up, not the fix. (c) Also right: playing the cue after the UI start does not change the gap. Android's runBlocking `play` delays every layer by the same amount. It stays in because it is harmless and stops a double cue under StrictMode, but I don't claim it as the fix. (b) Right, and real: the banner's entry was a withSpring of its own, started by its own effect, so it could land frames apart from the dim and the effect. (d) Right, and it matches 'first hit of a game': the dim is a plain view, while every effect is a Skia Canvas. In RN Skia 2.6.2 on Android, SkiaBaseView wraps a SkiaTextureView, so its picture shows only after onSurfaceTextureAvailable, then a Skia draw, then a TextureView layer update. On a canvas's first mount, Skia also pays its set-up, the shaders for what it draws, and the JS of its first mount. The banner mounts an SVG ring and an avatar. All of this makes the overlay and banner late compared with the dim, on the first hit only. Rejected: holding the shared clock until HitLayer is 'ready'. There is no signal for Skia's first draw. Fabric emits onLayout during the commit, before the native mount; Canvas onLayout is deprecated on Fabric; RN Skia 2.6.2 has no first-frame callback; and androidWarmup only rasterises the initial picture, which is transparent at alpha 0. items.fix: (1) The banner's entry now runs from the shared hit clock. A new worklet, bannerEnter(elapsedMs, reduce), in HitBanner.tsx gives the closed-form `settle` spring from rest (mass 1, stiffness 300, damping 30, from motion tokens), or a linear 200 ms fade under Reduced Motion. HitBanner's own useSharedValue / withSpring / withTiming effect is gone. The dim, the effect and the banner now all read one value in the same UI frame. (2) A new HitRehearsal (screens/game/hit/HitRehearsal.tsx), mounted by GameScreen next to HitLayer, pays the first hit's mount costs early. Only in a game with interferences (never in a practice, D44), from 2.5 s after the screen mounts (after the hit sounds' warm-up), it mounts one piece per idle moment, each for 250 ms: first the banner, then each allowed kind that has a Skia effect (fireworks, cats, warp, ink). items.test: In apps/mobile/src/screens/game/hit/__tests__/hitStartTogether.test.tsx (6 tests, all pass): (a) [new] HitLayer with a shared clock held at 0. (b) [new] bannerEnter: 0 at the start, more than 0.95 at 300 ms, never above 1.01, 1 by 2 s, and a linear 200 ms fade under Reduced Motion.
